content: Croscarmellose sodium is an excipient commonly used in pharmaceutical formulations. It is characterized by its high absorbency and insolubility, functioning similarly to a sponge. This property enhances the interaction between the active ingredients and bodily fluids, thereby improving the bioavailability of the drug. Chemically, croscarmellose sodium is the sodium salt of a cross-linked, partially O-(carboxymethylated) cellulose. Initially, it was utilized as a stabilizer in dietary supplements for horses. In pharmaceutical applications, it is an internally cross-linked sodium carboxymethylcellulose designed to act as a disintegrant. The cross-linking process reduces its water solubility while allowing it to swell and absorb multiple times its weight in water. This unique characteristic facilitates superior drug dissolution and disintegration, ultimately enhancing the bioavailability of the active ingredients in the formulation. Croscarmellose sodium also addresses several challenges faced by formulators, such as maintaining long-term functional stability, ensuring effectiveness at high tablet hardness levels, and overcoming issues associated with other disintegrants developed to improve drug dissolution. It is a widely used, FDA-approved pharmaceutical additive. In most tablet formulations, including dietary supplements, its primary role is to aid in the disintegration of the tablet within the intestinal tract at the desired location. Without a disintegrating agent like croscarmellose sodium, tablets may disintegrate too slowly, in the wrong part of the intestine, or not at all. This could significantly reduce the efficacy of the active ingredients.
